title: COVETOUSNESS
mv: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
mvp: ‘‘And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.’’ Luke 12:15
assignment: Mention five (5) sins that covetousness will likely produce. Hints are in the biblical examples in outline 1 (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Covetousness is a strong desire or an unpleasant longing to have something that belongs to another person. It is a wrong, insatiable greed for wealth that can sometimes manifest through envy. It is also personified as one of the deadly sins (Colossians 3:5). Covetousness is so dangerous that Jesus had to specifically warn believers to be on the watch for this vice and refuse to have anything to do with it. This will take a personal resolve with the knowledge of the consequences that follow covetous people.
Below are some biblical characters who exhibited covetous traits and the aftermath of their actions.

i: Achan coveted a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels' weight (Joshua 7:21) when they went to war with Ai after God had warned them not to take any accursed thing.
He brought defeat to Israel (Joshua 7:5); he admitted to having sinned (Joshua 7:20) and was stoned to death (Joshua 7:25).

Gehazi, Elisha’s servant, ran greedily after Naaman and lied to him because he coveted the gifts Naaman brought for His master, which he rejected (2 Kings 5:21-22). Gehazi and his generation got Naaman’s leprosy (2 Kings 5:26-27).

King David coveted Uriah’s wife, Bathsheba, and committed adultery with her (2 Samuel 11:2-4). That singular act led him to become a murderer because he initiated Uriah’s death (2Samuel 11:15, 24); he lost the child born by Bathsheba (2 Samuel 12:15-18), and God swore that the sword shall never depart from David’s house (2 Samuel 12:9-12).

King Ahab longed for Naboth’s vineyard; the latter refused, and it led to his death (1 Kings 21:1-3; 13). God took the kingship lineage from Ahab and, at the same time, pronounced a death sentence upon him and his family (1 Kings 21:19-22).

b.x: We can deal with covetousness in the ways stated below.

i: Ask God For Help: Like the Psalmist, there is a need to cry out to God for help (Psalm 119:36) against this dastardly act.
Be Deliberate: Staying off covetousness is an intentional act that starts with an individual. We must resolve to stay away from this vice (Deuteronomy 5:21).
Hate It: We must detest this sin in all the forms it may appear and fill our hearts with the fear of God (Exodus 18:21).
Stay Off It: We must avoid it like a plague or a cankerworm that is ready to destroy (Ephesians 5:3).
Mortify It: We must bring this work of the flesh under and subdue it (Colossians 3:5).
Be Pure: We must ensure that our discussion is without any iota of covetousness (Hebrews 13:5).

b.x: Staying off covetousness is a sign that you love others just as you love yourself (Romans 13:9). It also helps to prolong days (Proverbs 28:16) and averts divine judgement (Micah 2:2-3).

i: Mention four ways to deal with covetousness.
